analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 3305-3852), documentation of earlier releases that this PR did not change. The PR's only change is at lines 11-45, where it adds a v0.10.13 candidate section on Gemma 4 loop-exit and pair-setup stop handling. That hunk is outside the supplied units and its patch excerpt is truncated.

No code, workflow, config or threat-model file is changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no security regression. The excerpts contain no secrets or executable content.

Pre-existing behaviors described in the excerpts that fall under the threat model (T-041/SEC-035, T-059, T-060, TB-012) are not changed by this PR, and I did not restate them. These include the SSD prefix-cache TTL, maintenance and eviction behavior, the add-on hold socket hardening, and the release lanes. The changelog claims for the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup names and the add-on signer check are consistent with the T-041 and TB-012 descriptions as supplied.

Open question for integration: the v0.10.13 text in the truncated patch cannot be verified against code. It claims the Gemma 4 loop guard closes a thought and continues within the request's budget, and that a pair stop ends the leading Mac's start. The corresponding source changes (#2040, #2042) are not in this batch. They should be reviewed in their own units. They might affect T-010 cancellation propagation and T-041 cache donation, but nothing in the supplied evidence establishes that.
